probed.actRuleIntent: An iframe whose nested document contains focusable interactive content must not be excluded from the sequential focus (Tab) order. The fixture `
probed.whyStillWrong: Real barrier the harness still misses. The run5 fix at applicability-oracle.js:133 (`if (el.tag !== 'iframe' && el.tag !== 'frame') fams.push('keyboard-operable')`) deliberately STOPPED enumerating keyboard-operable on the iframe container, deferring 2.1.1 to "the frame's inner focusables on their own." But the collector's iframe-traversal (act-page-collect.js:395-430) records the inner `<a>` (`inFrame:true`, `focusable:true`) WITHOUT ever surfacing the parent frame's `tabindex="-1"` exclusion fact. So the only obligation built is keyboard-operable on the inner link IN ISOLATION. The trace confirms the wrong subject: `subject sc=2.1.1 xpath=/html/body/iframe[1]>>/html/body/a[1] ... verdict=NOT REPRODUCED` -> the LLM queried the inner link's AX node (role=link, focusable=true) and correctly said "no keyboard barrier is present" — because there is none ON THE LINK. The barrier (frame removed from tab order) was never given to any judge. No deterministic detector owns "iframe with negative tabindex + focusable content" anywhere in scripts/v3/lib. This is exactly the wrong_subject_targeted RCA R4 finding from run4 (RUN4-FP-FN-RCA.md:347), and the run5 patch addressed only the container-FP half, not the FN half.
probed.proposedFix: Add a deterministic 2.1.1 detector that OWNS the akn7bn fact, in the collector's iframe-traversal block (act-page-collect.js ~line 395) or as a build-v3 deterministic signal: when a rendered, non-inert, non-hidden top-level `<iframe>`/`<frame>` has a negative tabindex (`frame.tabIndex < 0`) AND the traversal collected >=1 genuinely-focusable inner interactive descendant that does NOT itself carry tabindex<0, emit a deterministic v3Barrier `{source:'deterministic', detector:'iframe-excluded-from-tab', sc:'2.1.1', xpath: <frame xpath>, authoritative:true}`. Gate precisely on the sibling fixtures: skip when `frame.hidden`, `frame.inert` (or `closest('[inert]')`), `display:none`, or collapsed (width/height <= 1, per Inapplicable Ex 3), and skip when the only inner focusable has its own tabindex<0 (Inapplicable Ex 4). This makes the iframe's tabindex the judged subject deterministically instead of the inner link in isolation.
probed.effectivenessCritique: Direction is unambiguously right and the fix WILL flip this case (the barrier becomes a deterministic authoritative v3Barrier, no LLM dependence). But it is over-fire-prone and must be gated against the rule's OWN inapplicable siblings, which I verified all share `iframe tabindex="-1"`: Inapplicable Ex2 `hidden`, Ex5 `inert`, Ex3 `width=1 height=1`, Ex4 inner `<a tabindex="-1">`, Ex1 inner `<h1>` (non-interactive). Two real traps: (1) `focusableByMarkup` (line 84) returns true for any `<a href>` REGARDLESS of its own tabindex<0, so a naive ">=1 inner focusable" gate FALSE-POSITIVES on Inapplicable Ex4 — the gate must exclude inner elements with negative tabindex. (2) the traversal loop never checks frame `inert`/`hidden`/collapse before descending, so Ex5(inert) and Ex3(1x1) need explicit guards. The `hidden`/`display:none` case (Ex2) is already saved incidentally because inner `visible()` returns false. Net: worth doing — it is a clean, spec-tight, single-rule deterministic win with no LLM noise, and the gate conditions are fully enumerable from the 10 fixtures. The only cost is the precision of the four guard clauses; get those right and there is no plausible real-page regression (a focusable iframe with negative tabindex holding reachable interactive content is a genuine 2.1.1 barrier in the wild too).

probed.actRuleIntent: 6cfa84: no element in sequential focus navigation (a tabbable element) may exist inside an aria-hidden="true" subtree. The fixture has <a href="#" id="sentinelAfter"> (focusable, no tabindex="-1") inside <div aria-hidden="true"> — the textbook FAIL ("Failed Example 6").
probed.whyStillWrong: Genuine barrier the harness missed. GT=failed (run4 case file: "expected(GT): failed ... polarity: recall"), and IBM's aria_hidden_nontabbable decides it a hard FAIL on /html/body/div[2]/a[1]. run5 root cause is twofold: (1) The ONLY deterministic 6cfa84 path is surfacing axe's aria-hidden-focus, but I ran axe on the fixture and it returns aria-hidden-focus as INCOMPLETE, not a violation ({"violations":[],"incomplete":["aria-hidden-focus","bypass"]}) — axe abstains because the <a> is off-screen (position:absolute; top:-999em). build-v3.js:305 `if (...|| f.kind !== 'violation' || f.review) continue;` skips incomplete findings for barrier promotion, so no axeObs barrier is minted. (2) The RUN4-RCA-proposed dedicated structural aria-hidden subtree-focusability runner (walk [aria-hidden="true"] for tabbable descendants) was never built — grep finds no such detector; only the axe-surface half (axe-surface.js:38 lists 'aria-hidden-focus') shipped. Net: v3Barrier(deterministic)=false, and the LLM only received the Close-button name obligation (RUBRIC 4.1.2 LIKELY_OK), never the focusable <a>.
probed.proposedFix: Build the deferred structural runner (a deterministic detector, e.g. in act-page-collect.js collection or a new lib detector consumed by build-v3.js): enumerate document.querySelectorAll('[aria-hidden="true"]'), and for each, walk descendants matching FOCUSABLE_SEL (a[href], button, input:not([type=hidden]), select, textarea, [tabindex], [contenteditable]) that are NOT tabindex="-1" and not themselves nested under an inner aria-hidden=false reset; emit each as a DECIDED 4.1.2 / name-role-value BARRIER on the focusable descendant's xpath (mint an axeObs-equivalent obligation in build-v3.js so it owns the barrier rather than routing the Close button to accessible-name-adequacy-v0). Honor the ACT focus-sentinel exception only for tabindex=-1 / JS-removed-within-~1s elements (which this fixture is NOT).
probed.effectivenessCritique: This WOULD deterministically flip this case: a static a[href] with no tabindex="-1" inside aria-hidden="true" is the exact, fully-decidable 6cfa84 condition; IBM and ACT GT both call it failed, and it does not depend on axe (which abstains-as-incomplete on the off-screen sentinel). The structural check is byte-decidable from the saved DOM, so no new evidence is needed. Over-fire risk is the focus-sentinel ~1s/role-of-trap exception: some legitimate dialogs put a tabbable sentinel in an aria-hidden wrapper and move focus off it within a frame — but the ACT rule's own exception is ONLY for tabindex=-1 or JS-removed-within-~1s elements, and a purely static scan cannot observe the ~1s JS removal, so a conservative static runner could in principle false-positive a dynamically-fixed sentinel. Mitigation: gate the emitted barrier on the element STILL being tabbable after page settle (the collector already settles), matching axe/IBM's own static decision. Given 6cfa84 is a coverage gap with GT-failed cases and the check is cheap and high-precision, this is worth doing — but it must be a deterministic structural runner, not another LLM rubric (the LLM was handed the wrong subject here).

probed.actRuleIntent: 0va7u6 "HTML images contain no text" / 1.4.5 Images of Text: applies to HTML images — INCLUDING elements carrying a CSS background-image — and fails when the image renders meaningful text that could be presented as real, selectable HTML text (and is not a logo/essential case). This fixture is W3C "Failed Example 3": a 500x200 <div> whose only content is background-image: url(.../0va7u6/textimage.jpg) — a JPEG of text with no real-text alternative.
probed.whyStillWrong: Genuine barrier the harness still misses. The applicability oracle never mints a 1.4.5 obligation for a CSS-background-image carrier. applicability-oracle.js:185 adds the images-of-text family ONLY when `IMG_ROLE.test(role) || el.isImage === true`; a bare <div> is role=generic with isImage=false, so it fails that gate. The background-image is instead routed at line 189 (`if (el.backgroundImageMeaningful === true) fams.push('non-text-content')`) to 1.1.1 ONLY — the comment explicitly excludes images-of-text: "NOT images-of-text/non-text-contrast (those need an actual graphic element)." The collector DOES nominate the div (act-page-collect.js:333-334: url() bg, no text, no accName, not aria-hidden, 500x200 not full-bleed ⇒ backgroundImageMeaningful=true), so the signal reaches the oracle; only the 1.4.5 routing is absent. Result: inScopeAutoPartial:0, inScopeObligations:0, outcome noObligation ⇒ recall miss on the GT-failed 1.4.5. RUN4-FP-FN-RCA.md line 346 already prescribes this exact fix; it was not applied for 1.4.5 in run5.
probed.proposedFix: In scripts/v3/lib/applicability-oracle.js, at the backgroundImageMeaningful branch (line 189), also push 'images-of-text' (and gate identically on not removedFromA11yTree), so a meaningful CSS background-image carrier mints a 1.4.5 auto-PARTIAL routed to the images-of-text-v0 rubric — not only the 1.1.1 non-text-content family. The collector already nominates the candidate and captures backgroundImageUrl, so the element-crop evidence is available for the rubric to judge text-vs-photo.
probed.effectivenessCritique: Would genuinely flip THIS case: minting the 1.4.5 obligation takes it off noObligation (inScopeAutoPartial 0→1), and the images-of-text-v0 rubric, handed a crop of textimage.jpg (pure text), returns REPRODUCED — a recall hit. The collector signal is already present, so this is a one-line routing change, not new capture work. Skeptical caveats: (1) FP/over-fire risk — every meaningful bg-image now also owes a 1.4.5 obligation, increasing auto-PARTIALs on decorative/photo heroes; but the collector already gates hard (no text/name, not aria-hidden/presentation/full-bleed) so the candidate set is small, and the rubric + non-authoritative PROVISIONAL disposition is purpose-built to return NOT REPRODUCED for photos/logos. (2) Residual evidence risk — the asset is a relative ../_assets path; if the crop 404s under file:// the rubric correctly returns PARTIAL (off noObligation but not a clean REPRODUCED), so the recall flip depends on the saved corpus mirroring the asset locally. Net: worth doing — the routing gap is a real defect with a documented fix and the regression surface is bounded by the existing collector gate and the conservative rubric.

probed.actRuleIntent:
Whether ARIA naming/description properties that are PROHIBITED on an element are absent — i.e. aria-label / aria-labelledby / aria-braillelabel / aria-roledescription / aria-brailleroledescription must NOT appear on an element whose role prohibits naming (here a bare

, implicit generic role). The fixture has `

I love Bananas

` — a braille naming property on a name-prohibiting element, which kb1m8s expects to FAIL (4.1.2).
probed.whyStillWrong:
The saved collection shows axe found literally nothing for this fixture: `"axe": { "violations": [], "incomplete": [] }` (raw.json:23415-23418), so the build-v3 axe-decided/checker-uncertainty obligation paths had no signal to mint from, yielding run5 `noObligation / inScopeObligations: 0`. Root cause is two-fold: (1) v3 DELIBERATELY does not enumerate the 4.1.2 ARIA-validity facet in the oracle — "the OTHER 4.1.2 facet — ARIA-attribute VALIDITY (aria-* prohibited on a generic element, ACT kb1m8s) — is deliberately NOT enumerated here ... axe's aria-prohibited-attr owns it" (applicability-oracle.js:139-142) — so the whole facet rides on axe; (2) axe whiffs on THIS case specifically because it models `'aria-braillelabel': { global: true }` (axe.js:14144-14147), so `aria-prohibited-attr` treats it as allowed-everywhere, while `aria-braille-equivalent` returns true (pass) since the

has accessible text "I ❤️ Bananas" (brailleLabelEquivalentEvaluate, axe.js:27113-27120). Net: no axe finding, no obligation, FN. (Sibling fixtures 17a785ed/358fa0b8 DO get an axe `aria-prohibited-attr` incomplete and a checker-uncertainty obligation, but were FN only because runLlm:false; ours never even reaches that path.)
probed.proposedFix: Stop relying solely on axe for the kb1m8s naming-family facet. In applicability-oracle.js, add a NARROW obligation branch (using the already-collected `ariaAttrs`): when an element carries one of the naming/description-family ARIA props (aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-braillelabel, aria-roledescription, aria-brailleroledescription) AND its (implicit/explicit) role prohibits naming (generic/paragraph/none on non-widget text, i.e. the ACT kb1m8s applicability), enumerate a 4.1.2 name-role-value auto-PARTIAL obligation routed to accessible-name-adequacy-v0 (whose lines 66-73 already know to read a prohibited-aria checkerHint as a value/validity barrier). This is strictly narrower than "all aria-*" and matches kb1m8s applicability; it does not depend on axe emitting anything.
probed.effectivenessCritique: Skeptical read: the fix would mint the obligation for THIS case, but flipping the FN still needs the LLM to call it a barrier AND the run to have runLlm:true (this measurement had runLlm:false, so even minting wouldn't have flipped run5 — it only flips a future LLM-on run). Two real over-fire risks the oracle author already flagged: (a) the naming-family props are extremely common on legit widgets/landmarks/regions where they ARE permitted, so the role-prohibits-naming gate must be precise (generic/paragraph/strong/em text only) or it floods real pages with auto-PARTIALs that depress specificity on every other SC's scoring; (b) aria-braillelabel/roledescription specifically are rare, so most of the benefit is on aria-label/aria-roledescription, which axe ALREADY surfaces as incomplete — so the incremental recall this buys is mostly just the two braille fixtures (this one + maybe c4a2fe12), a tiny slice. Given the WCAG audit memo treats this facet as axe-owned and the per-SC payoff is 1-2 fixtures against a non-trivial flood risk, the squeeze likely is not worth the juice; the honest label is a tool/evidence gap (axe's `global:true` model of braille props), best left as a documented known-miss rather than a new oracle branch. Worth doing only if a future LLM-on corpus run shows the broader naming-family-on-prohibited pattern recurs on real pages.

probed.whyStillWrong: The harness emitted outcome=noObligation / v3Barrier=false / 0 obligations / 0 LLM verdicts (results.json entry for 7cddc927). The fixture genuinely fails.
